answer: Every signal lamp is filled each night, and the oil book records how much each lamp took, so the light burns until dawn. A vault lamp claimed as filled fails the book: the oil must have been poured at the delta of the lamp, and a lamp never filled goes dark before midnight. Forging a winter of lamp entries means hiring a lampman, faking ninety nights and paying 5,700, while the lagoon entry in the oil book is checked at every signal failure, so a lamp whose oil was never measured is blamed for the first late train.
